adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Colombia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Colombia country overview fixes the national framework every visitor to Chocó stands under: consensual same-sex activity has been legal since 1981; a 2011 law bans discrimination based on sexual orientation; the Constitutional Court legalised same-sex marriage in April 2016, making Colombia the fourth Latin American country to do so, and same-sex couples gained joint adoption rights in 2015; the right to change legal gender has been recognised since 1993. It also describes a national LGBTI policy text covering rights in public education, health care, prisons and as victims of armed conflict, stating that national entities may not refuse to recognise same-sex couples — the armed-conflict-victim protection being the framework directly relevant to this record's frontier-belt dynamic where armed groups rather than departmental police regulate conduct and trans women are displaced from departments such as Chocó. The page carries no department-specific content, so it only supplies the framework against which the record's no-deviation assessment sits.

It also covers a national LGBTI policy text addressing rights in public education, health care, prisons and as victims of armed conflict — the victim-protection clause engaging this record's national-pattern risk framing, in which armed groups post kill-lists and enforce 'social cleansing' and nearly 50 queer and trans people were killed nationally by the 2025 date of reporting. The page contains no Guaviare-specific content, so it supplies only the framework against which the record's 'national conditions with thin institutional reach' assessment sits.
